AbstractText.Label: Purpose
AbstractText.content: Goiter is a major public health problem, especially in developing countries like Ethiopia. Hence, this study aimed to assess the prevalence and associated factors of goiter among children in Waghimra Zone, Northeast Ethiopia.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: A cross-sectional study was conducted from April 8 - 25/2015 in Northeast Ethiopia. A multistage sampling method was used to select 454 school children. Data were collected using a pre-tested structured interviewer administered questionnaire. Children were examined for the presence or absence of goiter based on the United Nation Children Funds, International Council for the control of Iodine Deficiency and the World Health Organization criteria. Sampled salts were tested for iodine level by using rapid iodized salt test kit. Data were entered using the EPI info version 7 and exported to the SPSS version 20 for analysis. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression models were fitted and adjusted odds ratio (AOR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) was computed to determine the level of significance.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: The prevalence of goiter was 62.1% (95% CI: 57.5-66.5%). Being female (AOR= 3.1; 95%CI: 1.562-6.082), a family history of goiter (AOR= 5.180; 95%CI: 2.432-11.033) and use of non-iodized salt (AOR= 2.2; 95%CI: 1.120-4.381) were factors associated with goiter among school children.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusion
AbstractText.content: The prevalence of goiter was high. Being female and a family history of goiter increase the risk of goiter in children, but using iodized salt was protective. Therefore, ensuring universal access to iodized salt and increasing the awareness of the community on iodized salt utilization is recommended.
